main_text.p: Tristes Camœnæ, quòd modo vermium Te fusacircum tanta tegit cohors, Straruoque lumbricis cubili Turpe iaces putribus cadauer? O qui corusco sydere pulchrior Nuper micabas, quòd rutilum nitens Pulsis renascentem tenebris Mane diem docet imminere: Aurora panso candida quod parens Monstrare gestit purpureum sinu, Sic te reclusum nunc olympi Verticibus cecidisse summis! Te, quem tremebant totius incolæ Orbis coacti seruitium pati, Sic sede celsa nunc ad imas Præcipitem graviore lapsu Ruisse terras? Nonne ferocia Tales superbi pectoris impotens Minas crepabas? Iam tumentis Imperij super astra sedes Ponam nitentes: Iam ferar ætheris Tractus per altos punicei super Conuexa cœli: Iam Syoni Iura dabo metuenda vitæ. Quo monte gentes conueniunt sacræ Clarosque nostris nunc procul arcibus Spectant Triones: hîc honores Hic mihi thura ferent sedenti

page.notes: Verse set in a single stanza without visible stanza breaks, so the whole poem is one paragraph with line breaks. "fusacircum" is printed run together and may be "fusa circum"; the spacing is ambiguous. "Straruoque" is uncertain and may be "Straguoque" or similar; the scan is faint here. "vermium" is printed with a mark over the m that may be a superscript abbreviation; it is read here as "vermium". No notes, catchword or signature are printed.
